Subject: POC: short window spike (10k RPS) - request for temporary credits

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — Momentum AI is ready to run a short, high-concurrency proof-of-concept to validate latency under realistic peak conditions. We plan a 3-hour focused run next Wednesday (Sept 2) that will simulate up to ~10k RPS with typical prompt sizes (~75 tokens average).

We need a temporary credit uplift or promotional allowance to cover the expected token burn (~5M tokens estimated) and would prefer the uplift to be provisioned 1 hour before the run so we can warm up.

Attached is our load plan (momentum_load_plan.xlsx). Can Redwood confirm:
- feasible to handle 10k RPS for 3 hours on hosted/Dedicated?
- any recommended model/quantization settings to reduce cost while keeping latency targets P95 < 350ms?
- process for granting a short-term credit top-up and required approvals?

Ops will monitor, and we can provide detailed telemetry. Appreciate quick guidance so we can finalize the schedule.

—Elena

Hi all — quick technical note after reviewing the load plan. Assumptions: average request 75 tokens in, 20 tokens generated (95 total), and 10k RPS sustained for 3 hours (10,800 seconds). That’s roughly 102.6M tokens — the original 5M token estimate looks low given those numbers.

Recommendations:
- Use our rwd-latency-1 model (4-bit quant) with prefix/KV cache warm-up. This should keep P95 ~250–320ms in our internal tests when batching and cache are used aggressively.
- For cost containment: set max_generation_tokens to 20 and enable per-session KV caching; run a 30-minute warm-up at 2k RPS before the spike.
- Credit suggestion: provision 120k free credits (promo) to be safe, but if Momentum prefers a smaller uplift we can do 50k with the understanding we may throttle once exhausted.

I attached a short estimate (connor_capacity_estimate.pdf) with token math and a recommended schedule. If you want, we can provision a temporary burst pool (engineers need ~4 hours lead time).

Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
